'''János Pach''' (born May 3, 1954)<ref name="epfl"/> is a mathematician and computer scientist working in the fields of [[combinatorics]] and [[computational geometry|discrete and computational geometry]].

==Biography==
Pach was born and grew up in [[Hungary]]. He comes from a noted academic family: his father, {{ill|Zsigmond Pál Pach|hu|Pach Zsigmond Pál}} (1919–2001) was a well-known historian, and his mother Klára (née Sós, 1925–2020) was a university mathematics teacher;<ref>[https://ematlap.hu/hirek-ujdonsagok-2020-12/1005-gyaszolunk-pach-zsigmond-palne-sos-klara-1925-2020 Pach Zsigmond Pálné (Sós Klára) (1925−2020), ''in Hungarian'']</ref> his maternal aunt [[Vera T. Sós]] and her husband [[Pál Turán]] are two of the best-known Hungarian mathematicians.<ref>[https://csanna.blog.hu/2013/12/05/sejteni_es_bizonyitani Interview with János Pach (2013), ''in Hungarian'']</ref>

Pach received his [[Candidate of Sciences|Candidate]] degree from the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]], in 1983, where his advisor was [[Miklós Simonovits]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy |id=15046}}</ref>

Since 1977, he has been affiliated with the [[Alfréd Rényi Institute of Mathematics]] of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences.<ref name=renyi>[http://www.math-inst.hu/researchers.html Research Fellows], Rényi Institute</ref>

He was Research Professor at the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]] at [[New York University]]<ref name="website">[https://www.math.nyu.edu/~pach/ Personal website of János Pach], New York University</ref> (since 1986), Distinguished Professor of Computer Science at the [[City College of New York]] (1992-2011), and Neilson Professor at [[Smith College]] (2008-2009).

Between 2008 and 2019, he was Professor of the Chair of Combinatorial Geometry at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne]].<ref name="epfl">[http://actualites.epfl.ch/presseinfo-com?id=538 János Pach appointed as a full professor of mathematics], EPFL, December 12, 2007.</ref><ref>[https://archiveweb.epfl.ch/dcg.epfl.ch/ Chair of Combinatorial Geometry, EPFL]</ref>

He was the program chair for the [[International Symposium on Graph Drawing]] in 2004 and [[Symposium on Computational Geometry]] in 2015. He is co-editor-in-chief of the journal ''[[Discrete and Computational Geometry]]'', and he serves on the editorial boards of several other journals including ''[[Combinatorica]]'', ''[[SIAM Journal on Discrete Mathematics]]'', ''Computational Geometry'', ''[[Graphs and Combinatorics]]'', ''Central European Journal of Mathematics'', and ''Moscow Journal of Combinatorics and Number Theory''.

He was an invited speaker at the Combinatorics session of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]], in Seoul, 2014.<ref name="seoul">[http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php List of Speakers at ICM.]</ref>
He was a plenary speaker at the [[European Congress of Mathematics]] (Portorož), 2021.<ref name="portoroz">[https://www.8ecm.si/programme/plenary-speakers List of Plenary Speakers at ECM.]</ref>

==Research==
Pach has authored several books and over 300 research papers. He was one of the most frequent collaborators of [[Paul Erdős]], authoring over 20 papers with him and thus has an [[Erdős number]] of one.<ref>[http://www.oakland.edu/enp/compute/ Computing Your Erdös Number]</ref>

Pach's research is focused in the areas of [[combinatorics]] and [[discrete geometry]].
In 1981, he solved [[Stanislaw Ulam|Ulam's]] problem,  showing that there exists
no [[universal graph|universal planar graph]].<ref name="P81">{{citation|
year=1981|
journal= [[European Journal of Combinatorics]]|
volume=2|
title=A problem of Ulam on planar graphs|
last1 =Pach|
first1= János|
issue= 4|
pages=357–361
|doi=10.1016/s0195-6698(81)80043-1|
doi-access=free}}
</ref>
In the early 90s<ref name="micha">[http://jointmathematicsmeetings.org/meetings/national/jmm/1908_invited.html AMS Meeting]</ref>
together with [[Micha Perles]], he initiated the systematic study of extremal problems on [[topological graph|topological and
geometric graphs]].

Some of Pach's most-cited research work<ref>[https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=author%3Ajanos-pach Google scholar], retrieved October 23, 2008.</ref> concerns the combinatorial complexity of families of curves in the plane and their applications to [[motion planning]] problems<ref>{{citation|first1=Klara|last1=Kedem|author1-link=Klara Kedem|first2=Ron|last2=Livne|first3=János|last3=Pach|first4=Micha|last4=Sharir|author4-link=Micha Sharir|title=On the union of Jordan regions and collision-free translational motion amidst polygonal obstacles|journal=[[Discrete & Computational Geometry]]|volume=1|issue=1|year=1986|pages=59–71|doi=10.1007/BF02187683|doi-access=free}}.</ref><ref>{{citation|first1=Herbert|last1=Edelsbrunner|author1-link=Herbert Edelsbrunner|first2=Leonidas J.|last2=Guibas|author2-link=Leonidas J. Guibas|first3=János|last3=Pach|first4=Richard|last4=Pollack|first5=Raimund|last5=Seidel|first6=Micha|last6=Sharir|author6-link=Micha Sharir|contribution=Arrangements of curves in the plane: topology, combinatorics, and algorithms|title=15th Int. Colloq. Automata, Languages and Programming|series=[[Lecture Notes in Computer Science]]|volume=317|publisher=Springer-Verlag|pages=214–229}}.</ref> the maximum number of [[K-set (geometry)|k-sets and halving lines]] that a planar point set may have,<ref>{{citation|first1=János|last1=Pach|first2=William|last2=Steiger|first3=Endre|last3=Szemerédi|author3-link=Endre Szemerédi|title=An upper bound on the number of planar ''K''-sets|journal=[[Discrete & Computational Geometry]]|volume=7|issue=1|year=1992|pages=109–123|doi=10.1007/BF02187829|doi-access=free}}.</ref> [[Crossing number (graph theory)|crossing numbers of graphs]],<ref>{{citation|first1=János|last1=Pach|first2=Géza|last2=Tóth|title=Graphs drawn with few crossings per edge|journal=Combinatorica|volume=17|issue=3|year=1997|pages=427–439|doi=10.1007/BF01215922|doi-access=free|s2cid=20480170}}.</ref><ref>{{citation|first1=János|last1=Pach|first2=Géza|last2=Tóth|title=Which crossing number is it, anyway?|journal=[[Journal of Combinatorial Theory]] | series=Series B|volume=80|issue=2|year=2000|pages=225–246|doi=10.1006/jctb.2000.1978 | doi-access=free}}.</ref> embedding of [[planar graph]]s onto fixed sets of points,<ref>{{citation|first1=Hubert|last1=de Fraysseix|first2=János|last2=Pach|first3=Richard|last3=Pollack|contribution=Small sets supporting Fáry embeddings of planar graphs|title=Proc. 20th ACM Symp. Theory of Computing|year=1988|pages=426–433|doi=10.1145/62212.62254|isbn=0-89791-264-0 |s2cid=15230919|url=http://purl.umn.edu/4760|doi-access=free}}.</ref><ref>{{citation|first1=János|last1=Pach|first2=Rephael|last2=Wenger|title=Embedding planar graphs at fixed vertex locations|journal=Graphs and Combinatorics|volume=17|issue=4|year=2001|pages=717–728|doi=10.1007/PL00007258|s2cid=36270095 |url=http://infoscience.epfl.ch/record/129229 }}.</ref> and lower bounds for [[Ε-net (computational geometry)|epsilon-nets]].<ref name="KPW92">{{citation|

==Awards and honors==
Pach received the Grünwald Medal of the [[János Bolyai Mathematical Society]] (1982), the [[Paul R. Halmos – Lester R. Ford Award|Lester R. Ford Award]] from the [[Mathematical Association of America]] (1990), and the [[Alfréd Rényi Prize]] from the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]] (1992).<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.math-inst.hu/renyi_dij.html|title=Rényi-díj|publisher=Alfred Rényi Institute of Mathematics|access-date=8 March 2010|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120904135121/http://www.math-inst.hu/renyi_dij.html|archive-date=4 September 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>[http://www.cs.sfu.ca/SeminarsAndEvents/LectureSeries/archives/000231.html Short biography] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080624130333/http://www.cs.sfu.ca/SeminarsAndEvents/LectureSeries/archives/000231.html |date=2008-06-24 }}, from SFU Computing Science.</ref><ref name="Academy of Europe 2014 Pach János">{{cite web | last1=Hasani | first1=Ilire | last2=Hoffmann | first2=Robert | title=Academy of Europe: Pach János | website=Academy of Europe | url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Pach_J%C3%A1nos | access-date=2022-12-19}}</ref> He was an [[Erdős Lectures|Erdős Lecturer]] at [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] in 2005. 
In 2011 he was listed as a [[fellow]] of the [[Association for Computing Machinery]] for his research in [[computational geometry]].<ref>[http://www.acm.org/press-room/news-releases/2011/fellows-2011/ ACM Names Fellows for Computing Advances that Are Driving Innovation] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111209030430/http://www.acm.org/press-room/news-releases/2011/fellows-2011/ |date=2011-12-09 }}, [[Association for Computing Machinery]], December 8, 2011.</ref>
In 2014 he was elected as a member of [[Academia Europaea]],<ref name="Academy of Europe 2014 Pach János"/> and in 2015 as a [[fellow]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]] "for contributions to discrete and combinatorial geometry and to convexity and combinatorics."<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/new-fellows|title=2016 Class of the Fellows of the AMS|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|access-date=2015-11-16}}.</ref>
In 2022 he was elected corresponding member of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences.<ref>{{citation|url=https://mta.hu/mta_tagjai|title= Corresponding members of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences|access-date=2022-05-21}}.</ref>
